scores.claim_text: Xometry's distinctive brand name should appear in US-listed-filer disclosures (counterparties, suppliers, customers, competitors).
scores.interpretation: Strong public-filing footprint of 175 hits. Top filings include both XMTR's own 8-Ks/10-Ks and (per heuristic 7) the brand has substantial real presence in EDGAR. PASS — brand exists and is real. Note: a deeper analysis would partition own-filings vs counterparty mentions, but 175 raw hits clearly clears the recipe threshold.

scores.claim_text: Thomasnet is a 'leading industrial sourcing platform in North America' covering 70,000+ industrial processes.
scores.supports: external_brand_validation recipe: 1-9 hits = MODERATE; here 15 hits but all top-10 are Xometry's own filings — zero independent counterparty corroboration of the 'leading platform' claim.
scores.interpretation: Total hit count is just over the PASS threshold (15 vs 10), but ALL top-10 hits are XMTR's own filings. For a self-described 'leading' B2B sourcing platform with 70K industrial processes, near-zero independent counterparty disclosure is a soft underdelivery — industrial buyers/suppliers don't appear to be referencing Thomasnet in their own SEC filings. Could simply reflect that Thomasnet usage is operational/marketing rather than disclosure-worthy; not a fraud signal, but tempers the 'leading' descriptor.

scores.claim_text: Xometry has proprietary AI/ML patents covering its Instant Quoting Engine, manufacturability analysis, and marketplace matching.
scores.interpretation: USPTO ODP shows 12 granted patents pre-cutoff with at least one match in claimed categories ({'ai_pricing_quoting': 0, 'manufacturability': 12, 'marketplace_matching': 0}). Real portfolio exists.

scores.claim_text: Xometry acquired Tridi Teknoloji A.S. (Istanbul, Turkey) on January 2, 2023.
scores.supports: named_acquisition: 13 hits in EDGAR including XMTR's own 10-K disclosures of the acquisition (and a small number from System1, an unrelated filer that happens to use the substring). Acquisition is consistently disclosed.
scores.interpretation: Acquisition appears disclosed across multiple XMTR filings (8-Ks/10-Q/10-K). Tridi is a private Turkish startup so external corroboration would be minimal by design (per heuristic 4). PASS.

scores.claim_text: Xometry integrated the Gravity Climate API into its marketplace in 2022 for carbon emissions calculation.
scores.supports: Per heuristic 4 (investment/tech partners often don't disclose); 3 EDGAR hits, all from XMTR's own filings, indicating internal disclosure of the integration. Gravity Climate is a private startup — external corroboration not expected.
scores.interpretation: 3 hits, all XMTR's own filings, consistent with the company internally disclosing the integration. The counterparty (Gravity Climate, private VC-backed climate-tech startup) would not be an SEC filer. PASS — claim is modestly disclosed and the absence of external corroboration is the expected baseline.

scores.claim_text: Xometry leases all of its US offices and does NOT own any real property — no owned manufacturing facilities. The company is a marketplace platform, not a factory operator.
scores.supports: Per heuristic 1 (EPA FRS = EPA-regulated facilities only; office/marketplace sites EXPECTED absent). 0 facilities is the correct expected result and CORROBORATES the office-only / marketplace business model.
scores.interpretation: EPA FRS returns 0 hits for Xometry in Maryland (HQ state). This is exactly what is expected for a software-marketplace platform that explicitly states it owns no real property. The claim and the registry are consistent — the company is NOT mis-claiming factory operations. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Xometry serves the Defense industry vertical; large defense primes (Lockheed Martin) are plausible buyers/suppliers.
scores.supports: named_counterparty_order recipe scoring hint: 0 hits = RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE for material commitments, BUT caveat applies: 'some commitments are immaterial relative to the counterparty's size.' Xometry never explicitly named LMT — this is an indirect inference from the 'Defense' vertical claim.
scores.interpretation: Lockheed Martin's filings make 0 reference to Xometry. Marketplace vendors are typically immaterial to a $60B defense prime — absence is consistent with normal procurement-disclosure patterns and does not contradict the 'we serve Defense industry' claim (which is non-specific). MODERATE — the claim is plausibly true but lacks any specific named-customer evidence.

scores.claim_text: Xometry serves Aerospace industry buyers (first-named industry vertical); Boeing is a plausible counterparty.
scores.supports: Same logic as C-007. Boeing CIK 0000012927 returns 0 Xometry mentions; counterparty is too large for a marketplace vendor to be materially disclosed. Xometry never explicitly named Boeing.
scores.interpretation: Boeing's filings make 0 reference to Xometry. Same calibration as C-007: marketplace-vendor-to-marquee-OEM relationships are typically immaterial-disclosure. The Aerospace-industry claim is generic and not falsified by 0 hits. MODERATE.
